name: Straight-Tusked Elephant
notes:
The largest thing that walks north of the Tethys. The tusks come out almost straight rather than curving, which is why a pair of them makes a doorway -- and why the Narmada archive, far to the south, has two propped either side of its own, carried down in trade. It lives in Mainland Asia and does not breed on Jambhudweep. The Narmada's straight-tusks are working animals, walked south across the Aravali crossing by their drivers, and the species keeps the valley's name only because that is where its bones and its worked kin were first set down.

Worked rather than tamed, and the distinction is one the drivers insist on: an animal that can put a shoulder to a cut block of basalt cannot be made to do anything it has decided against. What a driver has is forty years of being agreed with.
sources: Pleistocene South Asian megafauna, adapted to canon
journal_prompt: It is browsing at the height of a roof and has not registered you at all. The tusks are wrong -- they go forward rather than out, two pale shafts a shade longer than the animal is tall.
